notes.title: Birthdays in the Perumal and Sivan Koyils
body: Panduranga Bhaktotsavam Day 2; Garuda Jayanti; Sundaramurti Nayanar Guru Pujai

Panduranga Bhaktotsavam continues as ever, but the big event is Garuda’s birthday! This falls on Aadi maasam, Swati nakshatram. There is a 530pm Thirumanjanam, followed by an 8pm Sahasranamapujai, where the reading is done by a single priest called in for this, while Naresh Bhattacharya does the pushparchanai.

Next door in the Sivan Koyil, Sundaramurti Nayanar’s birthday also falls on Aadi-Swati. Guru pujas are simple affairs, all organized by the Siruthonda Nayanar Thiruthonda Sabhai. A simple abhishekam for utsavar and moolavar happens at some point in the day – if the evening is busy with other things, it will be in the morning. If not, it will happen in the evening. Then the utsavar is taken in procession around the temple, and brought to the garba griha for moksham or union with Sivaperuman. Then he is returned to the utsavar mandapam. At some point in the day, a group sits outside the Nayanmar sannadhi and sings songs–often in parallel with whatever else may be going on in the temple. But this is Guru puja, and it happens on all the Nayanmar birthdays.
There is a poster out front today announcing an auction of the deities' clothes in the coming days...

notes.title: Conversations
body: We sat at last with Thathacharya in his Saram house for some three hours this afternoon, hearing him tell stories, quote insightful lines, and generally guide us through both temple history, practice, and the Sri Vaishnava world of ideas.

He asked about us, and couldn’t place either of our “Tamil-ness.” I couldn’t tell if I was devastated by that or not. He and his wife run a strict Iyengar household. Sipped coffee cups were kept on the dining table, not brought into kitchen. Thathacharya has a meditation hall upstairs, and is a big fan of Srisri Ravi Shankar. Thathacharya started chanting prabandham in the temple past 50. He’s one daughter in Chennai, with a grandchild who’s 4 (whom we will meet on Avani Avittam day).

notes.title: Yoga Shakti Alankaram
body: Day 4: Nāḷ-utsavam. The alankara today is Yoga shakti. We’ve been chasing the alankara crew, but timings have proven unpredictable. Will have to keep at it.

notes.title: Alankaram-Abhishekam in Preparation for Aadi Velli
body: We stop by Mutthumariamman to ask about tomorrow’s alankaram, but are asked to stay for the evening’s abhishekam instead. This temple has a practice of finishing the abhishekam that typically precedes an elaborate alankaram the night before – then Jnanavel Swamy’s son works through the night getting the deity ready for the next morning. Tonight, he says the Ubhayakaras are coming in from Chennai and won’t mind if we stay – this isn’t a private temple, but many families have this as their kuladeivam, so it feels often like it’s the shrine of a specific group. The abhishekam happens late, close to closing time.

notes.title: Surprise, Surprise, It’s Annapurni in Rice Flour
body: 8AM Alankaram is ANNAPURNI, done with rice flour, the sari details marked out with almonds along the length and to show creases, walnuts and atthi or dried figs to show decorative and border details. Mutthumariamman had a spoon in her hand and a small pot with foil bunched in it to show pongifying rice I suppose. Sari beneath the rice flour alankara sari, border colour matched. Quite creative and ingenious. Jnanavel Swamy had refused to tell us the alankaram the night before, it’s meant to be part of the early morning awakening darshan. Suspense and surprise.

There’s also a vibrant alankara tradition at Vedapuriswara, but not nearly as creative as at Mutthumariamman. Chandana kaappu today in orange, but with pink glitz – Tripurasundari’s blouse was pink, sari details in the same shiny pink material.

notes.title: Amman Shrines Come Alive on Adi Fridays
notes.occasion: Panduranga Bhaktotsavam Day 4, Aadi Second Friday
body: We stopped in at Senkazhuneer Amman koyil, whose kitchens for pongal are HUGE, and by the kulam at the back. Seldal vizha today, full nadaswaram orchestra, but we didn’t stop to see it. Ther chasing in the evening on the way back from Angalamman, the place was a mini-mela. The phat-phat-phat-coconut breaking was interesting and happened once the ther had turned onto the main Vazhakulam road. Full nadaswaram and the Kailaya vadyam group leading the way.

Over at the Manonmani Theruvu Koyil on Canteen street, the grandson was there doing a simple alankaram which he decides with his mother, now that he has slowly taken over from his father’s passing away. We took photos and left. (Update, Navaratri time: we see an Iyer doing a single kaalam puja there, maybe the family has found someone to take care of the place more regularly than the grandson can? They don’t do much for Navaratri).

notes.title: 108 Paal Koodams for Angalamman
body: There are a few women making pongal in the morning, none at night. Several bringing what they made at home + the maa-vilakku from home – in all the Amman temples today.

10AM 108 paal kudam abhishekam: Not sure 108 were used, but you’ve to buy a 100rs ticket and then you get a koodam of milk – we saw women pouring the milk, so perhaps there could be more added. Then the koodams are decorated with turmeric and kunkumam, and their necks tied with neem leaves. They’re placed outside the Calcutta Kali shrine, a small puja with a kalsham happens there, and the women with tickets pick each one and the priest gets the one with the kalasa – they go out in procession, zig zagging through the streets. Before they depart and as they return there’s a deeparadhanai, and then the women (all chanting “Om shakti Parashakti”) come in via the central passage marked by guardrails, and the milk is poured over the deity. Soon a group gathers outside near the pranala (கோமுகை (Gomukhai) or நாழி (Naazhi) / நாளம் (Naalam)) to catch the milk that falls there. The pranala has been cleansed itself with turmeric and kunkuma, though the priest does have to stick a bar through its opening at one point. There’s an aradhanai. Then the alankaram in the evening is just silver kavacham, nothing like last week.

There are some young women like Charu who will ask me for photos, and who are participating in events like this for the first time. I see her at many pujas after this. Being at the temple and a part of its ritual life is clearly a path to womanhood in this area of town. Charu is not alone; the demographics of this temple are wide, and there are many young (and beautiful, and beautifully attired in saris!) women who join the pujas. The priests know this, and advise and coach accordingly.

notes.title: Vizha Wears On
notes.occasion: Agni Vasanta Thiruvizha Day 5, Aadi Second Friday
body: Amman is in a green sari holding shankha-chakra: She is Narayani most probably or Vaishnavi and tonight her purappadu is on a naga vahanam.

Some tension in the air today because the alankaram man wasn’t keeping to timings, and the priest was threatening to have him replaced with another. This man doing alankaram was trained by another, older man whom we saw at the Sivan koyil – I think he said his name was Rajasekaran. The present alankarar isn’t his son, but has learned from him for long and it’s been in this “lineage” for long.
Some women making pongal, off and on through the day. Not as many as we were told there’d be, but a steady flow.

notes.title: 24 Hours of Song
body: I’m not sure we do justice to this event with all the other running about we’re doing but the Panduranga Bhakta group has 24 hours of bhajanai outside the Panduranga Sannadhi starting today: Akhanda Divya Nama Bhajanai. We cannot help but notice the sponsors for this are the Vasavi Kannika group: Arya Vysya Kommmati Chettiars whose kula deivam is Kannika Parameswari.

notes.title: One Unknown Alankaram!
body: Draupadi amman’s alankara figure is standing in a pink sari today, but I cannot tell what her alankaram is. It’s day 6: Naal utsavam, and she will ride out on a Yaanai vahanam (elephant)

notes.title: Dhanalakshmi Alankaram
body: Day 7: Naal Utsavam. Morning abhishekams happen on all days, but without much ceremony. The evening’s alankaram is Dhanalakshmi.

notes.title: The Alankaram Transformation
body: Day 8: Naal Utsavam. After so much chasing, we finally managed to sit with the men doing the alankaram for the utsavar of Draupadi Amman for the four-odd hours they worked today. They turned Draupadi Amman into Mariamman today. It was fascinating to see the addition of limbs, body, chest– even if body proportions do get a little bit sacrificed. Not sure when these alankara traditions came into being or how they evolved. But this is about taking a small utsavar form and enlarging her so that She is ready for her vahana, which is usually many times her size. And it’s about creating recognizable forms, pathways by which the divine presence becomes accessible to those who can then know Her, at least outwardly like this.

notes.title: This Time, Annapurni on Video
body: Day 9: Naal Utsavam. Done with the photo-taking yesterday, not done with the fascination of the alankara process, I went to take video today of Draupadi Amman being transformed into Annapurni. Not much to say except that we had a hundred clips, played at 5X speed and turned into a 3-minute video, which became this high-grossing thing on Instagram, ha ha ha.

notes.title: Gajendra Moksham
body: In his previous birth, the elephant king Gajendra had been King Indradyumna, a great devotee of Lord Vishnu. Thanks to a sage's curse, he had been born as an elephant. One day, he was with his herd in the water when a crocodile grabbed a hold of his leg. A great fight ensued, but the elephant was not equal to his adversary. As he faced almost certain death, he remembered Perumal and raised a lotus flower with his trunk. He called out to Vishnu, offering Him the lotus and praying for refuge. His prayer is known as Gajendra Stuti — the hymn of Gajendra.
This story gets ritually re-enacted in the temple–this is pretty much the essence of Gajendra Moksham, as much as we can tell.

Perumal comes out of his sannadhi and goes around after the usual pujas to the kulam at the back of the temple, where the remainder of the puja takes place. I don’t realize the interest of this event, so I wind up there late when the place is already crowded and the best vantage points taken. I have no view at all, so finally manage to squeeze into the other end, much to the amusement of Sekar mama, who chides me for my lack of fore-planning. The puja as such is a simple affair. There are two brass forms of the elephant and the crocodile with his mouth open. The lotus is on the elephant’s tusk. He gets a small abhishekam along the way. At one point, the priest signals and there’s a burst of firecrackers on the far side near the washrooms.

And that’s really all there is to it. Perumal goes back, people go down to the kulam for theertham. Suddenly the view is completely clear to take photos of the ritual remnants, and the elephant and crocodile who seem much like props, now that it’s all over.

notes.title: Parashakti Alankaram
body: Day 10: Naal Utsavam. Not much going on here apart from the ordinary. The alankaram tonight is Parashakti.

notes.title: Rajarajeshwari Alankaram
body: Day 11: Naal Utsavam. The alankaram tonight is Rajarajeshwari.

notes.title: A Theruvu Koyil Has Its Brahmotsavam
body: 20ஆம் ஆண்டு ஆடி மாத பிரம்மோற்சவம் for the Manimutthumariamman Koyil near the Kamban Kalairangam. Ramanan Gurukkal had told me the schedule, but I thought it was an 8pm start and was getting ready for a day of writing when he called and asked if I was coming, so I dropped all and went. They were just getting started with the Ganapati homam, so that worked out well. 2 priests from outside plus the Gurukkal, who did the homam. The road was blocked off (with a cord and a small piece of cloth that looked like an Amman dress on either end), a pandal set up, large set up for homam. Actually beautifully done – Ganapati homam, Mahalakshmi homam, Mariamman moola mantra japam, Astra homam (can be a few types, Pashupatastra being done for Siva pujas, in this case Shakti astra homam which brings about samharam of bad/evil “black magic” influences – priest said. The um-phat was emPHATic). Very participatory process, after the basic swaha offerings were made, then the homa plate went around and every one put in the fire a little. The gurukkal’s mudras were a delight to watch; he does have very long and elegant fingers.

The general Amman Koyil setup was interesting to witness. A yellow cord connects the Kalashas with the agni kunda. There are three kalashams, and the central one with the face of the Goddess. Gurukkal goes between the agni kunda and the kalashas, there appear to be rather more mudras repeated than we see at other temple homams. At times, he’s acting in sync with the other priests, offering flowers or using the mudras to “complete” a set of ritual actions. Once the homams are done, Amman abhishekam happens, performed by one of the invited priests. The gathered women meantime prepare the bamboo pole that is the temple’s dvajasthamba by cleaning it, applying turmeric and then putting kunkuma pottus. Gurukkal comes to add mango and neem leaves, jasmine etc. Meantime the invited priest has climbed up to the stucco Parashakti figure, and I think done some clearing and put a new sari on Her. The kalashams are taken by appointed people to the garba griha, and used to pour on the amman and her trident. Then the simple yellow flag is brought out and tied to the kodi maram. It’s sprinkled with kalasham water – as am I – then after some mantrams and flowers, it’s raised and fixed in a waiting bag of sand. Everyone there has their hand in it. It’s a nice moment, which the photos capture well, if I do say so m’self. Soaked daanyam or seeds are put into the soil of the bag that now holds the kodi maram.
Prasadam is chakkara pongal and sundal. I’ve no transport, so I walk home. It takes me less time to cross town and get near the ashram than I think.

notes.title: Naga Puthalam Alankara for the Whole Garba Griha
body: Abhishekam for Mutthumariamman would have happened the night before, but now the morning is here and the whole garba griha space has been used. Vinayaka utsavar is standing in front, all covered with flowers. Anthills with snakes on the ground. Amman in full chandana kaappu, with a big Mala of limes on top, Thazhampoo “petals” like spikes over her, neem leaves to cover any last space on top. Quite something. Took them till 5am, Jnanavel Swamy said. Naga putru or puthalam (sacred anthills)--a reference to the emergence of Shakti forms from the Naga worlds beneath.

notes.title: Somewhere Between Craft and Ritual
body: 10am-noon is Sapta Kannika puja at the Kannika Parameswari temple. Seven Kannikas were prepped the night before by the Mahila Sangam, readied for today’s prayer. 8 committee members all there, evidently pleased and proud of their work. The ladies were all taking so many photos the priest scolded them and reminded them that rahu kaalam would soon be upon us. Then there commenced the usual floral puja. The temple was full by 1145am, when I left. All ladies. The old sweet lady I sometimes see there may not be from the community as she said “I only take flowers if they give me” – but many made an effort to give me as usual and to include me. They’re sweet and tight and generous.

notes.title: Ekadina Laksharchanai
body: Ekadina Laksharchanai (100X Sahasra), Archanai going on in 3 different kaalams spread through the day for the utsava murti (7-9AM, 9-11AM, 5-7PM); the older priest reads Lalita Sahasranamam.

I (Deepa) got to angalamman 730am. A moola mantra japa homam is just finishing in advance of the laksharchanai to the very alankarified utsava murti. Plastic malas and all. Pongal making is also happening simultaneously at the back of the temple. Utsava murti is alankarified and sitting out, so the kunkuma archana happens there. Elder Gurukkal reads from a sahasranamam, Lalitha namavali he tells us later. Following this – deeparadhanai, shodasha upachara, more chanting+archanai, a lovely moment when the nadaswaram plays just for Her (the players were good today), and a final deeparadhanai.

There’s a special abhishekam at 10am, and a Karaga vizha just after. The family that had undertaken this pledge was present, 3 boys, plus a lady who must have been the grandmother of at least the littlest boy with the beautiful face, and a young girl, likely his sister. The grandmother was given an Amman form with a trident across her tongue, and she almost instantly went into a trance. Pambaikarar was a man like Senthil pusari at Angalamman, who accompanied the family carrying the karagam the whole way, all around the block, barefeet in blazing heat, too much to bear in spite of wearing socks and several people pouring water to cool their feet. The pambaikarar priest did the lime dhristi in quite a dramatic way several times. The photos capture that somewhat well. After their return, karagams brought down again, and this time the granddaughter in purple got into a trance-dance. Then koozh and kanji were distributed, and all wiped clean, the rush was incredible.

This evening is a kumbha padayal, followed by a veethi ula which started around 9. Not sure what the alankaram was, She had a trident. The kumbha padayal was… masalamasala and strange. Ramanan gurukkal gave me a big pot to take home and I have to return the plastic vessel. It had been set up on several long tables beforehand which were being washed and cleaned when I got there – so much rice on the road, gasp. The woman who had been part of the karagam group asked me if I had been “called by amman only this year” or if I’d been coming before. The former, I said, going with her phrasing.
*Why do people say “govinda govinda” almost instinctively while karagam is being raised etc.? Some story we don’t know or just a transfer of Perumal koyil habits?

notes.title: Amman Pirappu Utsavam
body: It’s day 12, and today Draupadi Amman’s birth from fire is celebrated, so it’s called a pirappu utsavam, or Agni kundathil pancāli, Panchali who emerges from the Agni kundam. Moola Amman is also in chandana kaappu, showing her birth in fire, and there’s tamarind rice, sweet pongal covered with ghee to make a mirror in which Amman’s reflection can be seen in the middle (neyyi kulam, not so effective though maybe too much light?), lemon rice on the right, curd rice dotted with pomegranate on the top. Different team did alankaram. Happens again on Tuesday before Thirukalyanam, I’m told.

Draupadi was out in two forms – the utsavar ready for purappadu, and the wooden Amman. Fire, too, was of 2 sorts – electric lights and a red cloth blown to look like fire, also a real fire in the homam clay “pot.” Pothuraja lifted twice up and down from the fire. Then Amman – the wooden utsava – with lights out, twice. It was quite stunning. Crowded today, with many offering maavu vilakku and pongal.
All of it took very long, nearly till 845pm, but was well worth the wait.

notes.title: Arakku Maligai Eritthal
body: Day 13: Naal Utsavam + Arakku Maligai Eritthal, or “the burning of the lac palace”--which refers to an Bharatam episode in which Duryodhana and plots to kill the Pandavas by trapping them inside a palace made of highly flammable materials. This happened after the Purappadu returned, though, so I wasn’t around to see. It took place at the cutting of Bharati, on the way back to the temple at 1030pm. Kannan sent me the photos you see.
Today’s Alankaram was Rajakumari.

Manimutthu mariamman had another bath this morning, in anticipation of the noon Annadanam and evening Unjal utsavam. I went at 11ish, the alangaram was with nool malai for amman, tables set up for a major sappaadu. Cooking had happened since early that morning, applams fried on spot. A wide range of people, from the destitute to the certainly undeserving, sat waiting. A clearly impoverished and sick pair of women came, one of the temple nirvagam people applied vibhuti on their faces when one claimed to have found all in the Amman – a gesture of some kindness as it was a physical touch. There was a muslim man there I think with his wife. I think this was the Ubhayam of the lawyer A. Rajarajan, who’d also been there from the start. I left after the deeparadhanai at 12:30 for Ojas’ grandmother’s 13th day shrardha chaappaadu. Kasturi mami called me to come for lunch, but how could I possibly, today.

In the evening, Dyuman drove me to the Unjal Utsavam. Some of the men who’d been around all through were there, one looking like he might be slightly drunk–others were ignoring him. I got my photos and left. The request for photo-sharing is quite intense in this group! I’ve had to say I’ll send them to one representative, and they share.

notes.title: Bakasuranukku Annam
body: Day 14: Naal utsavam, Carrying annam to bakāsura (bakāsuranukku annam kondu porkkuthal)

*Sunday Aug 2 Panchali alankaram. Usually it’s Angala Parâmeswari on this day but it was decided otherwise this year. Partibhan’s mother said Andal alankaram but that wasn’t so even though it’s recorded as such in photos.

*5-6pm Veerappan Swamy was doing his daily storytelling but at the Mariamman temple near the clock tower in Muthialpet. Stories of Bakasura. Right when he was done, you could hear the approach of the procession from Droupadi Amma, led by the man with the Parai and the Sunddu Kucchi-Adi Kucchi. No other instruments. Everyone came walking except the priest’s teacher friend (I think they returned together). The women at the temple had clearly been waiting for this. Big drums of sambar saadam and everyone had dabbas and bowls to take some. Chaos. Fight broke out between local boys, threatened to get big — fitting, for a bakasura feeding. I got scolded for not caring about that and taking photos. All the ladies were super nice and posed when I asked to take photos. The men doing the doling out, too. Simple little deeparadhanai, and then the doling continued, this time off the thattu vandi. When it was done – it was done. I walked back home with the thattu vandi.

notes.title: Karaga Thiruvizha
body: Day 15: karaka thiruvizha, malaiyidu alankaram

The new chariot the priest has been speaking about was to have arrived today at 3pm but didn’t there was a death, so it got delayed a day. Alankaram is மாலையிடும் (Maalaiyidum) – because she’s a new ponnu getting married tomorrow she has a garland for her groom. Sweet!

Karaga thiruvizha – I photographed the karagam making process extensively. Basically it’s a copper pot with spokes and a frame that allows flower malas to be strung on it in a particular way. One done, it was carried by Prakash accompanied by the other men to the Sivan koyil kulam – there they bathed, get ready there by smearing chananam etc., wear sacred thread, Rangaradjou swamy ties the kaappu, then there’s a puja and aradhanai, and the veera jati session happens in the back prakaram near the entrance to the kulam. 3 whips per man. Priest then picks the karagam, dances with it, returns it to Prakash who carries it out and back to the temple. It’s all quite the scene for the otherwise very sedate Vedapuriswara Koyil.

notes.title: Vil Arangettram and Thirukalyanam
body: The day’s schedule reads: Day 16: Ādi 19: 930 vil arangettram, 1030am to 12 thirukalyanam for Draupadi and Arjun – but that title hides so much!

Wedding notes: major crowd, super interesting morning. Amman’s wooden figure goes on procession with the big bow. They stop at the corner of Bharati and Iswaran, and along comes Arjuna, dancing. Meantime Veerappan bhagavatar is telling the story of the wedding and the contest with the bow – absolutely splendid, see the recording. We clap when Jarasandha, Karna, Others fail to string that bow, he says, because their success makes more room for Arjuna who is the rightful groom. The bow bending by Arjuna could be more dramatic, but once that’s done, the deities move back to the temple and the wedding proceeds. It’s a splendid community affair. LOTS of women in attendance, and what a scramble for bangles at the end there.
The new ther finally arrived at 6pm, clearly with some fanfare, which we missed. Priest remarked on it later. Kalasa was kept in the garba griha when we saw it. Hoisted a day later in the evening.
Thanks to the Bhagavatar and his storytelling, this was easily my favorite day of this whole vizha so far.

notes.title: Offering Pongal, 108 Times Over
body: (Rahu kalam): 108 Pongal offering 2pm onwards cooking, after 3-530 or so puja. Very delayed. Arun went. The first pot of pongal that’s set to cook seems to be the temple’s own. It is placed in front of the maha balipeetham. Neelakantha Gurukkal lights the fire himself and lifts the pot onto the stove. Bhaktas trickle in after 4pm and pongal stations prop up along the western and northern prakarams. By 5pm, the cooked pots begin to arrange themselves in the Gayatri mandapam, awaiting the late arrivals’t completion. By the end there exactly 11 batches of pongal, including the temple’s own pot and another one in the temple’s madapalli. Once completed, the priest collects a ladle of pongal from every pot into a single bucket. After this, the helping priest takes another pass, this time collecting coconut water from the bhakta’s coconuts and returning the two halves. Soon after, an aradhanai and archanai complete the puja.

notes.title: Andal Utsavam Gets Going
body: This will continue until Aadi Pooram, for 10 days. (Andal shares the birth date of Kannika Parameswari?) Adhyapakas recite Andal pasurams only in the AM after thirumanjanam, evening none after 6pm. They only recite from Thiruvaymozhi. 3 times pradakshina, once mallari, twice keerthanas.

notes.title: Arjunan Thavasu and Simha Vahanam
body: I’m not sure what I missed today, but I was told to take photos of the little Arjuna standing atop a tall spoke. That showed up later at the crossroads where the bow was kept. Some of these ritual events are better enacted than others, suffice to say.
Alankaram today was Durga of course, on Her Simhavahana.
Day 17: Ādi 20: Nāḷ-utsavam, Arjunan davasu (penance), Singhavāhana Mahishasuramardini

notes.title: Virata Parvam and Kuthirai Vahanam
body: Today’s schedule was Day 18: Ādi 21: Nāḷ-utsavam, Virāta Parvam (Madu Pidi Sandai), AM abhishekam, (Puducherry Yadava Marabinar)
It rained this afternoon so we went and saw the alankaram (Veera Panchali on the horse vahana, sitting sidesaddle, all ladylike) and left but didn’t return.

Today’s stories would have been from Bharatam Book 4, about the Pandavas hiding in disguises in the kingdom of King Virata, the Kaurava raid on his cattle, Arjuna revealing his identity, the completion of the year incognito. No enactment of it, it seems. Veerappan bhagavatar said he sang the mangalam and the nadaswaram played along very well – and it was special, but I missed it. Heartbreaking for me. I hope I get another chance. The Nadaswaram players have complained that their music is often drowned out by the sounds of the mechanical drums – odd that both are played simultaneously, creates a bit of a din. But at times like this when they voice their complaint, it is taken into account and that’s nice.
The schedule lists a noon Annadanam, but no sign of it having happened.

notes.title: Pecchayiamman 1008 Limes Archanai; Murugan Abhishekam and Purappadu
body: 1030AM Murugan Abhishekam was a simple affair, on the occasion of Krittikai. We went and Arun got photos. Lawspet and Ghousiga also marked this, morning abhishekam and evening ul-purappadu, and Ghousiga probably did a veethi purappadu, with Aadi Krittikai being one of three special Krittikai celebrations. Mutthumariamman Alangaram was on a Mayil vahana, with a lime malai.

In the evening is a Lalita Sahasranama and 1008 lime archanai for Pecchayiamman. When I go, there is an anda full of limes in front pf Pecchayiamman, plus piles of limes at her feet, it is a namavali recitation and ½ hour puja after which the limes are distributed. No photos allowed there, so I got an idea of the puja and ran fast as I could to Perumal – to catch the karagam coming out from the sannathi and leaving to the theemidi ground from there.

notes.title: Rathotsavam and Theemidi, the Day for Which We’ve All Been Waiting!
body: What a day. Got there am when pongal was being made, and people were coming for sedal and veeraa jati. Archana happened, annadanam outside. Vahanas were out – one for Perumal, one for Arjuna, the ther for Draupadi amman. While all this is happening, we talk for a few minutes to Veerappan Bhagavathar, and record him on video as he tells a story that involves the emergence of Kootasuran from the ashes of a burned Kamadeva. He quotes Alf Hiltebeitel’s From Senji to Kurukshetra (takes me a hot minute to recognise that it’s in fact this work he’s quoting). Saying this is how he understood some of the connections in the Villu Bharatam.
(Were there not just two vahanas in the am? The two that went to Muthialpet. One with Dharmaraja, Arjuna, Pothuraja and [Sahadeva perhaps?], and the other with Draupadi on the lion?)

1030am or so, the ther with the minor figures (Pothuraja + 2 others?) plus one with the wooden figure of Draupadi amman go to the Mariamman temple ground near the Muthialpet clock tower. The ground had become a “legal issue” said the priest and asked us to take video of the crowds, even giving Arun permission to climb on the Draupadi vahana. Someone else had parked their ther there, and had only moved it to one side because they went and complained the night before.

This is the scene of the battle when the sons of the 5 pandavas are killed. Aravan’s head witnessing the Mahabharata is in one corner. Rudra chor or Rakta chor is prepared and shown to him, mixed with the aid of a neem branch. 5 veshtis are laid out – 3 on the east end, 2 on the west, one in the middle on a bench. Men are there with tambulam offerings – why? Designated men receive the priest’s permission and lie down on each, are covered with another veshti, the rakta chor splattered on top, and other men behind them start shaking their bodies and saying the names of the respective son. Then there is more veera jati that happens, with the priest wielding the whip. The men are lifted and carried off.

Action moves to the side where there’s a form of Duryodhana in the sand, with marbles in specific places (they are much sought after later). A deeparadhanai happens and draupadi amman’s chariot goes over his body and then proceeds to the theemidi ground, so that the nerupu making can start. The ground is near the Ginger hotel, a horrid Vaaikal (canal) running beside. People are coming in numbers to put wood bunches in the fire. A man called Senthil Kumar befriends us, and takes us to his home which overlooks the scene. He says we can return in the evening. This is the ground that apparently the Draupadi Amman koyil was compelled to move the theemidi to after a child died in the festival during French times. It’s TN-Pondy border, so they could do as they wished here.

[Cop asks me: you’re at all temples taking photos, are you from here, where do you live, are you doing this alone or for someone. I told him, he seemed satisfied. Another cop later expressed appreciation for what we’re doing. The man (priest?) near the Arvan head practically blessed us. Took photos with him and family, whom we’ve met at the Sivan koyil.]

The Ther departure from the Koyil is a major Kailaya Vadyam event. Unstoppable. Amman, Perumal, Arjuna come out and do a round around the temple, with tonnes of neem leaves thrown on them as they move. It all takes a long while though. Ther is ready to go but late, close to 5pm. Rangaswami comes, delays it more (on the street), and there are trees to cut and wires which cause many pauses and delays. The deeparadhanai for all 3 processional deities is a dancing affair, a big group is there with drums and cymbals. They’ve to cut a service tree branches, they get stuck at the Athithi hotel crossing bc of worry of a HT wire, movement is very slow. The ther probably reaches around 8pm or later.

Meantime, karagam is prepared again. Prakash has a bath, comes down 1 floor to pray to ancestors, then comes to receive the karagam – the drummers go inside, there’s a dance as usual, and then they wait for news of ther. Arun and I dart off to Angalamman, I stay there, he returns because Narayanan tells us to come right away – this is 720pm. From there the karagam departs for the perumal temple, goes in the front way, into the sannathi, deeparadhanai there, comes out, proceeds behind the ther which is still on the Muthialpet/MG road visible in the distance. Traffic is a nightmare. We take backroads, stop for food, wind up there – quite late, as it turns out. Karagam reaches, men walk over the nerupu and presumably return to the temple from there directly.

Karagam party storming into the Perumal Koyil seemed to me to be the most sacred moment of the day. The phrase that comes to mind: “an invasion of the Infinite” – Sri Aurobindo of course means it as an invasion coming down from the Infinite into the mind, but the experience yesterday was of the inverse. An invasion from down to up. Something very violent and true about it.

*Prakash is Ramradjou’s younger brother’s son. Ramradjou has 2 daughters, so the nephew has to continue the lineage. He’s been doing the theemidi for many years and carrying the karagam for about a decade.

The ther itself stopped at the end of the street far north of the theemidi ground. Only Arjuna and Perumal came to the theemidi ground and once everyone was done, they made a quick return. We got there much too late. Were waiting to see if Senthil would let us to his balcony, but before we could the man who had described Mariamman’s sari as “radium” (green), found us out of the blue, asked if we’d taken photos, and took us deep into the crowd. We had less than 10 mins – and it was done. Had he not shown us the way, we may have missed entirely the very thing we’d been so anticipating. I’m still quite struck by that help that came out of nowhere, and the near miss we had, in a sense.

Ther returned to the pandal made for it at the end of Thiagaraja st. and the brass statues stayed at a house nearby (opp 71, the house with the women who always had water out for Perumal processions. The lady talked to me today Aug 8, she had me pegged as a researcher).
The published schedule:
Day 19: Ādi 22: Rathotsavam (Chariot Festival) & Thee Midhi (Fire-Walking) Festival
6:00 AM: Kālai 6.00 Manikku Abhisēgam, Prasādham Viniyōgam
3:00 PM: Pagal 3.00 Manikku Thēr Purappādu.
2. Padukala Utsavam (Sacrificial Battlefield Festival), neruppu kuzhi, vādikkattuthal
3. Fire Lighting Ceremony (Neruppu Pōdhudhal)

notes.title: A Homam That Wasn’t
body: Shodasha Lakshmi homam, Sahasranama recitation typically and with a vilakku puja in the evenings. (In the model of the Candi Homan, something to do with vegetables.) We didn’t see it, since it appears it wasn’t done at all. Priest told us on 6th August that they would do nothing.

notes.title: Gendhapadi Utsavam
body: The day after the Ther vizha, Draupadi amman’s chariot comes to roost at a small makeshift pandhal near the Perumal Koyil. It remains there till the next morning. Then, this is the schedule:
Day 20: Ādi 23: Kenthapadi/Gendhapadi Utsavam: At Thiyagaraja Street, erecting a pandal for Abhishekam, flower decoration, and Prasadam distribution. The Chariot procession departs at 7:00 PM.

There is a very quick abhishekam for the 4 deities – Draupadi, Perumal, Arjuna, Pothuraja – which we missed, that’s how fast they did it. Needed to get it done so that they’re ready with alankaram by 7pm said the priest. I guess nobody wanted the delays of the previous day! Simple alankaram. Full meal prasadam comes from the Perumal koyil madapalli. Boys on this street are the ubhayakaras, and they’ve organized it. They seemed in charge the whole time, and came by at the start of the deeparadhanai for special blessings from the priest.

*why only kunkuma abhishekam for this amman? We have some time to talk to Ramrajdou swamy. He has seen the Kamakhya yoni being given a kunkuma abhishekam in the temple in Assam. Asked there if it could be done for any amman. Was told there was nothing wrong, it could. So he does it now only for the moolavar, never for the utsavas. So this is a practice not randomly brought in on a whim but on the authority of the practice in Kamakhya, and a sign of how these customs evolve and change in “conversation” with each other.

*priest and a helper talking about the ther route for this evening – starts from MG, goes all the way down to Govindasalai and then back via Anna Salai?? Or how? The concern was about the height, and preparations for wire cutting etc.

*parai notes: 2 kucchis, fatter one is sindu, thinner one is kucchi. They represent talam and naadam. Sindu illamal kucchi velai seiyaathu, kucchi illamal simbu velai seiyaathu – he parai is played with two sticks: one long, thin flat bamboo stick (approx. 28 cm) called 'Sindu/ Sundu Kuchi' and a short, thick stick called 'Adi Kucchi' that can be made from any variety of wood (approx. 18 cm)/ Adi kuchi. The man playing (in photos) is Kuppuswamy, and this is the 4th generation of players for this temple. He called it rajavadhyam, which I took to mean played ahead of Rajas – which is what he said. But rajavadhyam as such means “king of instruments” and can just as easily be applied to the nadaswaram.

In the evening – The ther is still parked at the northeast corner of Perumal Koyil. It’s going to leave from the ubhayakara’s house to go in procession around town. Departure time announced – 7pm. Time it eventually left – 830pm. Although meanwhile, from 720 onwards, preparations began. A table was brought before the deities; loud movie-style songs of Mariamman and Murugan blared, with coloured lights flashing from a mini-truck. The scene was also graced with the amusing presence of a lion and a gorilla mascot to whom all children flocked. A few members of the Nadaswaram team were visibly disappointed by these unceremonious additions. Prakash’s father also was evidently disappointed. Prakash arrived soon after with the Karagam from the temple on his head. Upon the table, a padayal was offered to the deities. Aradhanai, archanai, followed by the deities being carried to the ther up the road. It was a short walk stretched long – very slow, swaying steps for the deities, accompanied by the drowned Nadaswarams faintly audible due to the speakers blaring their own music. Perumal and Arjuna cross MG road and board their respective vandis. Draupadi Amman is hoisted once again onto her regal seat in the ther. Aradhanai for all three in the same sequence, and finally the ther pushes off. The Karagam is placed on Arjuna’s vandi and completes its procession on that seat.

I watch the ther cross MG road – exactly 15 meters – which takes well over 20mins because of the unending traffic caused by Home Minister Amit Shah’s visit to the town. I plan to have dinner and return to catch the ther on Nehru street. But gates of heaven open upon the Perumal-led crew, and all plans are washed away.

notes.title: Manjal Neer Utsavam
body: Day 21: Ādi 24: 9AM Manjal Neer utsavam, arava bhūpati moksham

After what must have been a long and rain-washed night of procession, the ther returns to the temple at around 8 in the morning. I’m told that the deities will leave for the aravan moksham at Muthialpet by 930. Perhaps it’s here that the Manja neer utsavam gets its name, from the abhishekam? Because nothing else in the day’s events explains it.

930 arrives, but the post-abhishekam alankaram still going on for Draupadi Amman in the sanctum. Another hour goes by. 1030 arrives, when Bhagavatar sir calls me and says nothing will happen until evening. He is very kind and offers to call me when the procession begins. The priest tells me the same as I take leave.

My phone rings at 415pm. Bhagavatar sir informs me he is leaving for the ground. At 430 I go to the Ajanta signal and unfailingly find the purappadu on their way. They reach the ground by 445. Once in the ground, the vandi placed so the deities face South, towards the temple’s side entrance. There’s a naga shrine alongside a stone figure with a hand-drawn face who I’m told is Pidari Amman. Potthu Raja is placed near Aravan’s head, and Bhagavatar takes his seat next to Potthu Raja. He recounts the story of Aravan’s birth through Arjuna and Uloopi, his watching of the great war, and his subsequent rebirth and slaying of Kutasura (who is born of the ashes of Kama).

A final Aradhanai for Aravan, Potthu Raja, and Draupadi-Perumal-Arjuna. Aravan’s head is taken off and wrapped up in a towel, placed at the back of the deity-vandi and taken back to the temple. Sundal Prasadam that I share with Bhagavatar. Over.
Was it today that the Kodi came down? Oddly enough, it must be so but we’re not sure. The Patrikai is no help in this matter!

notes.title: Dharmar Pattabhishekam
body: Day 22: Ādi 25: 730pm to 930pm Arattin Ādi Ārambham, Dharmar Pattabhishekam

The simplest Pattabhishekam I’ve ever seen. Dharmaraja was in the ardha mandapam, got a crown there, and another one for the alankara murti who was Dharmar himself. No major ritual, only a little chanting.

Arun went in the morning, and saw the singing/chanting during Thirumanjanam: Andal Pasuram (Neeraattal Pasuram– but this is not Andal, so that’s confusing) and Panchasuktam of the Veda. After Thirumanjanam, while Alankaram going on: Thiruppavai.
Evening event was as usual, Thiruvaimozhi saattrumurai and 3 times circumambulation.

There was a 430pm Durga Puja today, Ram Murkoth’s Ubhayam. Every Tuesday lighting lamp to Durga is a vaaram utsavam at this and the Chetty Koyil. We didn’t go, but the process is the same as the first Brahmotsavam preparatory puja, which was to Durga in the same fashion.

notes.title: Unjal Utsavam
body: They don’t call it Vidayatri, but that’s what it is after the Kodi comes down. There were dance performances which caused the nadaswaram player Venkat some annoyance, as the unjal time is meant to be for nadaswaram but he said the priest’s right hand man is the one organizing such events. Amman alankaram sitting and her new husband lying beside her, as though just off her lap. Lots of ceremonial mariyaadai happening, starting with the Bhagavatar (naturally). We left midway as it felt increasingly like an acknowledgment event.
Schedule: Day 23: 730pm to 930pm unjal utsavam

notes.title: Kadal Theerthavari, or Great Gatherings
body: We went bright and early to Angalamman, and found the priests doing rounds with 2 boys, washing all the deities with water, getting them new clothes, flowers etc. Older priest doing the moola murti. Purappadu finally happened at 7:30am after circling the prakaram and a deeparadhanai outside, all supplies tucked into a bucket at the back of the vandi.

On the eve of August 15, there were major marching drills happening at the Gandhi statue. All the deities assembled at the far corner, closer to tennis ground. Angalamman from town was already there. The rest of the list Arun compiled:

list: Chetty – was supposed to come, according to Govindarajan who came with the Lawspet priests instead – but they hadn’t arrived by the time we left, close to 10am.

body: The process was basically the same as for a koyil abhishekam, including kalasa preparation, initial pujas, recitation during the pouring of substances etc. Each temple did this to their means, some of the amman koyils seemed to include kunkumam as the ground was red but I didn’t see this for myself. After this, the nadaswaram players accompanied the astra murtis being carried by priests to the water – the point is to immerse, but the waves are very rough, and though there were lifeguards present, I don’t think anyone went that deeply into the water. Some older priests with less of a retinue just went, washed, came.

Vedapuriswara and Perumal were the stars of the show. They arrived together, stood side by side, went down to the water together, and posed for photos after together. Wow :) Very, very wholesome moment with the two coming together - a sense of all the worlds coming into harmony.

Angala Parameswari had her usual Unjal Utsavam in the evening and new moon ceremony. Not sure what new moon ceremony there was, but the unjal utsavam was a little more dressed up than usual. Pandhal with white hanging feathery things. Crowd was more, for sure. Nadaswaram here always plays popular flmy songs, nothing very classical at all

notes.title: Parashakti and Mutthalarajan Share a Padayal Day
body: It was supposed to happen like this:
Day 24: Parāsakti Amman Padayal
Day 25: Mutthalarājan padayal

But the Parashakti event was postponed from yesterday on account of it being Pournami or because everyone is at the end of their tethers, I’m not sure which. But it happened in the course of the day. Kannan sent photos.

Around 830pm, food was laid out for Mutthalaraja. Parasakti Padayal was finished in the morning itself apparently, we didn’t know. Six banana leaves heaped with steamed rice, then covered in a variety of nonveg kuzhambus – seemed to consist of fish and chicken, then decked with boiled eggs. And of course, beer and some other kinds of alcoholic drinks placed at Mutthalaraja’s feet. An array of new faces at the temple. People thronging for the food. There is a bhajanai group singing. My intentions of asking them about what was being sung after the puja got washed. Chaos broke loose the moment the aradhanai was over. One entire band of people rushed towards the padayal with buckets and dabbas in hand, while another band rushed to find seats at the dining service arranged at the back. Some who couldn’t make it to the chairs, grabbed banana leaves and settled on the floor. Through all the shouting and commotion, I also manage to hear the alankaram-priest and another of his helper-priests arguing over the alleged disappearance of the “big bottle of beer”. Yikes. I exit.
Aadi pooram is Kannika Parameswari’s Nakshatra naal, so at 730am she gets an abhishekam.

We go around 830. Post-abhishekam alankaram done. Ladies setting up the Mandapa – there are dozens of hanging bangles and birds made of coconut leaves–this is their take on the valayal kaappu alangaram. The woman in red is the creative genius behind this. A photograph of Andal is in the middle of it all; after all it’s her nakshatra naal, too. We have prasadam and leave, but the remainder of the puja will happen no doubt in the same pattern as other Kannika pujas – with women sitting with plates of flowers while the priest chants, or doing their own parayanam while he does his.
This initiative is of the World AryaVysya Mahasabha Mahila Vibhag.

notes.title: Thiruvadi Pooram Abhishekam and 108 Shankhabhishekam
body: 6AM Thiruvadi Pooram Special abhishekam
6am, no signs of an abhishekam. All quiet. I go back at 730, and it’s all done. Seems to have been a simple special abhishekam.
10:30AM 108 Shankhabhishekam

I go after seeing Perumal-Andal abhishekam. Shankhas being given out to ladies as they line up to enter the moolasthanam. Sriram Gurukkal fills water and a blade of dried arugampul (I think) into every conch. The homam kundam is to the left and in front of Nandi, with the Kalasa at its head to the West. There is also the large and final Shankha, already prepared and kept.
6PM Thiruvilakku pujai–this is supposed to happen, but postponed to next Friday!!

Fabulous Valayalkaappu alankaram. The sheer scale of it blows one away. Not allowing photography of it is a crime. We only managed photos of the bangles that had been assembled a day before at the vahana mandapa at the back.

At Kamakshi Amman, usually there is a Valayal thiruvizha, during which the astra murti goes to the temple well, then is adorned in bangles. But not this year. Only abhishekam was done, followed by deeparadhanai. Very crowded around noon, as we pass by.

notes.title: Parasakti Valayalkaappu and Theerthavari
body: Vedapuriswara: Valayalkāppu; Morning around 10 am abhishekam will be performed for parashakthi amman and theerthavari will be held for her. Later the deity will be taken for procession inside the temple and will be made to stand straight to face the moolavar Tripurasundari. Deeparadhanai will be performed for both the main deity and utsavar deity. The bangle offering ceremony to utsavar will happen, offered by ubhakaras, Evening unjal utsavam will be performed for utsavar amman, bangle offering from devotees (info from Narayanan at Vedapuriswara, who turns out to be spot-on.)

We miss the unjal in the evening thanks to Perumal holding us back, but see the very last tail end return of Parasakti to her chamber. Mahalakshmi sannathi at the back has a puja going on. Chandana Kaappu for her, presumably in connection with Andal, with women queueing up for Archanai. The shrine is beautifully lit, with just vilakkus. Surreal sight.

This is Andal’s Janma Nakshatra naal, of course. The scheduled 7am purappadu begins around 8. Simple affair, Perumal and Andal walk out and left, straight towards the Mandapa on Sankardas St. Once there, aradhanai and curtain closes. 1030 abhishekam, done by 11. We stop by a little past noon, hoping to see the aradhanai. But it has still not begun, so we decide to let it be and come back for the 7pm aradhanai. Thathacharya spots us and calls us out later for not coming to the aradhanai! Oops.

Little did we know that Perumal and Andal would soon be shifted back to the temple due to a suicide down the road, thanks to which the deities cannot remain there anymore. The aradhanai happens around 8 at the temple, with everything else after that being delayed as well. By the time we are finished with the prasadam, which was given in meagre quantities because prepared only for the small crowd that would have been at the mandapam, it is already past 830pm. We decide drop into the Sivan koyil for the unjal utsavam (which we miss) and catch Perumal and Andal on the road again. We notice that everything at Perumal had been slow today, including the purappadu itself, stopping for a significantly longer time at the houses where people come out with archanai thattu.

notes.title: She Is Manonmani on Pooram
body: Sri Siddheshvari gets a special alankaram for Aadi Pooram. Most beautiful alankaram figure I’ve seen. Seems to have been made entirely from scratch, which is quite the process worth documenting in itself. Followed by a puja, done with utmost elegance and conscious intent by the priests. Very gratifying there, as always. There’s even a little Meru, covered in tossed kumkum and flowers–a navavarna puja.

Manonmani alankaram (the priests tell us later) with head tilted slightly and body at an angle, legs coyly placed – superb. Done in-house, using chandanam to create correct face proportions so that the body can look correct, unlike the typical alankara we see elsewhere. Kunkuma Abhishekam. Seems to be a combo of Sanskrit And Tamil? (name of devi + “Om haam” & after that Tamil and potri vasippu).

We arrive around 730 and find the curtain closed, with a bunch of people standing outside. Curtain opens and the boy priest hands out valayal to the ladies. Small archanai. Over. Alankaram looks very impressive for such a little place. All done by the boy. He seems to be very sensible and perceptive. One of the ladies hands him a saree, which he places across the headdress of the amman very well, keeping harmony with the rest of the alankaram.

notes.title: Lada Chinna Amman’s Aadi Pooram
body: In the morning, the lady with shop outside Manakkular was there doing abhishekam (simple, water, milk) and flower alangaram. She spoke about how people of all castes and religions would come for the elephant Lakshmi, but since her passing that has changed.

Went to Draupadi Amman, need to collect pen drive and give photos to priest. He gave us a lemon from the karagam, kept in a near-perfect fresh state from 10 days before. Claimed it had cured his daughter of incessant menstrual bleeding. Lemon as a thing with “uyir” which protects, absorbs negative/evil eye forces. Not used in this temple as a “head” of the deity. Talked again about his bypass, how he survived it and needed more procedures which they (family) rejected. Do you have faith in God, asks the physician (Kadavul mela nambikkai irukka) – to which Rangaradjou laughs and says “why I have a God who has faith in me!” (Yenmela nambikkai veccha kadavule irukkale!)

66th Brahmotsavan didn’t happen thanks to the planned Kumbabhishekam, but there is still an abhishekam-alangaram daily, starting today August 18 (would ordinarily have been the day of preparatory pujas) and livestreamed here (Britain Tamil Bhakti).

notes.title: Pondicherry’s Oldest Amman Koyil
body: We met Satish Gurukkal at Ellaiamman, to get some broad context on the temple even though it’s under construction and no utsavam is happening. He spoke a great deal about the once-importance and then decline of this temple, due to corruption and loss of land and property. He also keeps the existing ubhayakarars in play, by doing the pujas they have committed to and sending them photos, prasadam etc. It’s the only way that continuity gets maintained. Temples going through Thiruppani like this face existential risks of the loss of their established bases of support.

notes.title: Manakkula Livestreams

notes.title: Thiruvilakku Puja, a Week Late
body: 6PM Thiruvilakku puja, postponed from Aadi Pooram which was last Friday.

Simple puja, ladies buy a ticket, come set up lamp on banana leaf, rice, with vettrilai-paakku, banana, vatti, flowers to suit their tastes, oil, wicks, a little turmeric vinayaka bangles, kunkuma, pasupu. Bell, arati thattu. Coconut. Puja done first to vinayaka (nirapeksha murti, which refers to his formless, temporary status, gone after visarjanam), and then a kunkuma archana to the lamp while the priest reads the Lalita Sahasranamavali. Deeparadhanai to the utsavar, who is decked with thazhampoo today, and the puja is basically done. Kunkuma taken home to apply on aathukarar’s nethi :)

No homam or purappadu clearly. Only ubhayakarar puja in front of the utsava murtis, aradhanai, prasadam and over. Shankarnarayan Chettiar and another moustached person are here among the ubhayakarars. The event is live-streamed daily, for today it’s here (Britain Tamil Bhakti). Sridhar Gurukkal is in this video, chanting at about 6 minutes in.
Poster outside the temple reads:
Sixty-sixth Annual Brahmotsavam (18.08.2026 முதல் 10.09.2026 வரை)

On the 21st of the month of Ani, 05.07.2026, on Sunday, Panchamithi, Sataya Nakshatra, and Siddha Yoga, the installation of the Moolavar Vimana Balastapanam, the installation of the Parivaramurthigal Vimana Palastapanam and the inauguration of the temple were held smoothly with their great support from 10.00 am to 11.30 am. Therefore, as per the rules laid down by the priests, we would like to inform you that in this year's (66th) sixty-sixth Brahmotsava festival, the Swami Veedi Utsava will be omitted and the Swami will be anointed and adorned with incense and worshipped.

The Brahmotsava festival will be held for the sixty-sixth year from Tuesday, 18-08-2026, on the 1st day of the month of Aavani in the Parabhava year, to honor the Lord who has graced the temple with the divine name "Arulmigu Sri Manakkula Vinayagar" and has bestowed blessings upon the devotees who come and worship him. We request all the devotees who are witnessing this to come and have darshan of Sri Vinayaka and receive his blessings.
Temple priests: U.K. Ganesh Sivacharya, U.M. Srinivasa Gurus, J. Nagarajan Sivacharya and Palaniappan Temple Administrative Officer and temple staff.

notes.title: Aavani Moola Utsavam, Man Sumanda Thiruvilayadal
body: This is Narayanan’s family utsavam. The schedule is as follows:

list: 10AM Offering clothes to temple priests and servants (We didn’t see this, but saw the clothes there, names marked out for distribution)
1030AM Deeparadhanai, Chandrasekara puja/ carrying soil to Chandrasekara
11AM Theerthavari, performance of Sri Sokkanath Peruman carrying earth and mahadeepa pradhana at the temple kulam – this is the Man Sumanda Thiruvilayadal

body: They’re late to start. We spend the time singing with Subramani.

Utsavar comes out with Sokkanatha alankaram, taken to the kulam, abhishekam happens – then Guru mama introduces, the Manikarar tells the story sings (Here’s part of what he sang), and there’s a ceremonial filling mud in the pot on sokkanathar’s head. This is a tradition from Madurai, brought into this temple.
பண்சுமந்த பாடற் பரிசு படைத்தருளும்
பெண்சுமந்த பாகத்தன் பெம்மான் பெருந்துறையான்
விண்சுமந்த கீர்த்தி வியன்மண்ட லத்தீசன்
கண்சுமந்த நெற்றிக் கடவுள் கலிமதுரை
மண்சுமந்து கூலிகொண் டக்கோவால் மொத்துண்டு
புண்சுமந்த பொன்மேனி பாடுதுங்காண் அம்மானாய்
But he sings more, yet to transcribe.

“Pann-sumanta song” means a song containing musical modes (paṇ); “He who bestows a fitting reward” means the one who graciously grants an appropriate reward; “He who has a woman occupying one half” means the one who possesses a form in which a woman abides on one side; “the Lord” means the Supreme One; “He who dwells at Perunturai” means the one who resides at Tirupperunturai; “He whose fame fills the heavens” means the one whose fame is such that even the inhabitants of the celestial world praise him; “the great” means one possessing greatness; “the Lord of the vast sphere” means the Lord of the earthly world; “the God whose forehead bears an eye” means the God whose forehead bears an eye. Let us sing of the glory of our Lord, who, in bustling Madurai, carried earth for the woman who sold puttu, received puttu as his wages, and was struck by that king—the Pandya king—and whose golden body was consequently wounded. Let us sing of the glory of that wounded, golden body in the form of an Ammānai song.

When the saint-poet came to speak of the greatness of the Lord, he proclaimed with full voice that he was “one whose fame fills the heavens” and “the Lord of the vast earthly sphere.” But when he came to mention the Pandya king, he referred to him merely as “that king” (akkoval), deliberately alluding to the king’s lowliness. The story of the Lord carrying earth is related in the Kīrttit Tiruvakaval, Thiruvasagam Chapter 2.
Thus, what is being expressed here is the Lord’s immense compassion. Some notes:

list: பண் (paṇ) = a musical mode or melodic type in ancient/classical Tamil music; hence paṇ sumanta pāṭal means a song endowed with musical modes.
பெண் சுமந்த பாகத்தன் refers to Siva’s Ardhanariswara form, “he who has a woman occupying one half [of his body].”
மண் சுமந்து கூலி கொண்டு refers to the famous Pittu-vilayitta episode: Śiva takes on the guise of a labourer, carries earth for the old woman who sells puttu, and accepts puttu as his wage.

அக்கோவால் மொத்துண்டு means that he was beaten by that king—the Pandya king. The commentator stresses the contrast between the exalted descriptions of Śiva and the deliberately dismissive “akko” used for the king.
புண் சுமந்த பொன்மேனி is literally “the golden body that bore wounds,” referring to Siva's body after being struck.

notes.title: Pavitra Pratishtha
body: Came in to all 3 priests performing homam, recitations broadcast on microphone. Then off Mic, they each go to their respective agni kundams & chanting continues with the koorcham. Hard to make this out. Curtain closes presumably for prasadam which prasanna brought in long before & bells ringing, more chanting then there is a dhoopam deeparadhanai

Once the homam is done, the head scarf/turban is tied for the main pavitra priest, then colored pavitram is taken and chaattrified for the main murti, then Narasimha, Kodanda Rama, then Panduranga, Thayar, all the kalasas in the Yaga shala, Andal, Alvar sannathi, Garudan, finally Hanuman. After this the plainer yellow pavitram is tied to all the main temple stucco figures, gopuram, vimanam, dhvajastambha etc. Naresh bhattacharya did a surprising amount of climbing. Arun noted his dancer-like feet. (The priests were joking about putting the pavitra mala for the “Thamarai”--an oblique reference to the BJP).

At some point before the colorful pavitram is tied, the thin yellow pavitram is taken to the main shrine and tied as a mala and esp on the hands of the main deity and utsava figures. With all the bells and whistles. I think this happens before the priest wears the green turban and not after.
Then, swami purappadu, and the murtis are brought into the yaga shala to witness the next homam
One more homam kalam follows – pancha suktams – Purusha suktam, Narayana Suktam, Vishnu Suktam, Sri Suktam, Bhu Suktam/Durga Suktam + whatever other chants.
This is followed by the poorna ahuti, 3 poornam baskets circle the yagasala and then their contents are dropped into the central fire.
Archanai for the ubhayakaras, small deeparadhanai, prasadam (sweet pongal, puli saadam, thair saadam).

Thathacharya tells me Namakam Chamakam is part of the daily homam routine, but Ramanan Bhattacharya. says not a chance. So it appears the next homam kalams simply follow the same routine. . Why is Durga suktam chanted?
The tenth canto of Srimad Bhagavatam reveals the connection between the Supreme Lord Krishna and Goddess Durga, while narrating the divine advent of Krishna.

Durga (Yogamaya is the Lord’s internal energy, and Durga devi is her expansion) is born to Yashoda, and exchanged for Krisna when he’s born to Devaki and Vasudeva. So she is Yashoda’s daughter, Krishna’s sister, to be known and honored in many forms: Durga, Bhadrakali, Vijaya, Vaishnavi, Kumuda, Chandika, Krishna, Madhavi, Kanyaka, Maya, Narayani, Ishani, Sharada and Ambika
If Durga is Krishna’s sister – and Andal is Krishna’s wife, then Durga is Andal’s Nathanaar (!!!!)
And she is the one to give clothes to her sister in law at the time of her wedding. So says Andal in Nachiyar Thirumozhi (aaru patthu-la moonam paattu) 6.3:
இந்திரன் உள்ளிட்ட தேவர்-குழாம் எல்லாம்
வந்திருந்து என்னை மகட் பேசி மந்திரித்து
மந்திரக் கோடி உடுத்தி மண-மாலை
அந்தரி சூட்டக் கனாக் கண்டேன் தோழீ நான்
Indra and the entire clan of gods arrived,
approved me as his bride and chanted sacred verses.
Antarī* draped me in the bridal garment
and placed the bridal garland about my neck.
Such a vision I dreamed, my friend (trans. Archana Vencatesan, p163)
*Antari is Durga. More detail on this song

Later, Thathacharya remarks on the 143 verses – asks us what 143 means, ஒரு எழுத்து, ரெண்டு எழுத்து, மூணு எழுத்து – and I’m stumped, and he says “I LOVE YOU” because there’s a 143 pattern there also and the நாச்சியார் திருமொழி is a love letter to Perumal (first one is an entreaty to Kama to unite her with Perumal).
I burst out laughing when I heard this. You told it in a modern way, I said. It needs to be told in a modern way, he replied.

Nataraja Abhishekam, which happened very quickly early morning to mark Aavani Thiruvonam–THE Onam of the year. When there are bigger pujas going on (in this case Pavitrotsavam), even events like these are somewhat unceremoniously completed.

Pavitrotsavam proceedings took most of the morning. Homam started, only Venkatesa Gurukkal around. Deities lined up for abhishekam. Pavitram removed from the main kalasa and put in a basket for Guru mama. Siva Ambal abhishekam happened. Then the pavitram was taken into the main garba grihas and put on the main deities. Abhishekam for the utsavars happened. After that, the kalasa purappadu – carried by Thirukumaran and the other spectacled priest who’s usually around the Durga sannathi. Thirukumaran went into the Siva Sanandhi, the other went to Ambal. Since the abhishekam and alankaram had already happened, kalasa water was poured mostly on yoni and ambal’s feet (it looked like). The main table kalasas went first and then the others as well though we didn’t see them being moved in spite of being right there. Utsaavars had a simple flower alankaram and clothing, deeparadhanai for them after the final one in the main sannathis. We left just before this finishing.

Mesmerising purappadu energy at night. Colourful pavitrams worn only by the purappadu Swami and Ambal. All other deities and murtis have yellow pavitram, except the utsava murtis who were out for 3 days. Those have none. This was the very first Sivan Koyil purappadu which was a shouldered one–only “thol.” No vandi, Swami Ambal went on a big pallakku.

body: Aavani Avittam, it being pournami. Men at the kulam at the back – puja at home, bath in the kulam being auspicious as Thathacharya said, it’s completed here and the poonal changed. The poonal as we know is yagnopaveetam. Yagna + upaveetam which is “covering”. I wonder if there’s a link between this and the “chattaradu”/saattrumurai/ saatthupadi.
On Yagnopaveetham
On Yagnopaveetham as being a Pavitram

Ganesan sir later tells us there is no particular need to change poonal on this day, but it’s to do the Kanda Rishi Tarpanam that this is done – and the Tarpanam is a prayascitta, like the Pavitrotsavam. This is also the period of “veda arambham” so closing one learning cycle and opening another.
Morning homam only on the two square kundams, unlike yesterday which was only in the circular one.

We leave and intend to return for the theerthavari which is happening by the time we return. Long “spout” into which ghee is poured, the offerings include fruits and vettiver are walked around the andal sannathi and then one by one “touched” to the spout and offered. The final yellow cloth in fact is just soaked in ghee and offered. Roaring, beautiful fire. After this, Perumal and entourage return to the garba griha and doors close. By now it’s already late, we wait until 130/2pm, doors still closed, so we have to leave, presuming what follows is “only” the (alankaram and) saattrumurai.

The murti who goes for theerthavari looks like the selvar (Vishwaksenar) who went for the purappadu on Brahmotsavam flag hoisting day. And seems to make sense for it to be Vishwaksenar as an astramurti equivalent for Perumal.

notes.title: Karaga Vizha and Alagu Sevai
body: Ramanan Gurukkal alerted us to this event. We went to Lawspet Murugan Koyil around 9am, and found the whole group from the Veerabhadraswamy Chowdambika temple there with Karagam, and from there the procession wound through the town and returned to the Murugan temple and then “home” via the main road (going past the temple in the middle of the road). This is a festival of the Devanga Chettiars, who are originally from parts of Karnataka and Andhra, but long settled as weaving communities in parts of Tamil Nadu.

A group of dancers from Salem leading the way, along with musicians. A hollow-sounding thavil and Nadaswaram greatly out-sounded by other instruments and sounds. Priest was Panrutti Krishnan, coming alongside the Shakti Karagam, which was guarded by two men holding long knives in an X across the front. Traditional body flowers are also X across front and back, as in the Draupadi Amman tradition, too. Many stops along the way, either at homes (archanai thattu) or otherwise, while veera kumaras (who had had their kaappu tied at the Veerabhadra temple early am) took swords and made their promises to Amman, while hitting themselves a lot (or a little) with knives. Someone holding a tray with pandaram (a turmeric mixture though I only saw turmeric) to sprinkle on the wounds. Dancers may have been a paid team, but they were often hitting and bleeding, too. And they all had kaappu tied. Priest “spoke” to the deity multiple times, a particularly dramatic style of prayer that addressed Her by name (Iswari, Shambhavi, Bhadrakali, Jagadamba…) and then also seemed to ask “will I not do . XYZ” – eg. Dandam pettava? Addressing the men I suppose, Will you not bow down/ do dandam? To which the crowd answer was “bal-re” which one old man explained as the equivalent of Christians saying “amen,” an affirmation. This call and response was the mode of “speaking” throughout. “Shakthi Chamundi Jyothi amma Baa maa” – is the line used in other processions, similar utterances here. Lots of lime-camphor turmeric arati-drishti, happened multiple times. At one place, women came to wash feet and apply turmeric-kunkuma. Priest would also pick up swords periodically and “perform” before continuing to walk again. At one point, he sang something I think from the Abhirami Anthadi, perhaps the same as was being sung in the Sivan koyil – so this was the only Tamil, in addition to the Telugu and somewhat Kannada sounding chanting call-response.

Re-entering the temple, the chants were different again, going around the prakaram before going into the garba griha, again different and followed by “Raa, Amma” multiple times. Men of all ages, kids maybe 10 years or so, not all experts, but learning. Lots of room for novices. See this for more.

Returning, the priests go to the Draupadi Amman temple next door, about a block away, to fetch water. In an older time, this might have been from a well or a kulam, but it’s interesting that the “theertham” comes here as with the Draupadi amman temple from a different location, a nearby (allied?) temple. Though in both cases, people seemed to storm in, do their thing, and leave with no participation as such from the attending priests. The large rounded mud pot is washed, spread with turmeric paste, marked with Siva’s ash tripundra tied with rakshai, adorned with yellow samandi flowers, betel leaves banana offered, vatti, small archana, fruit coconut prasadam given to the ubhayakaras presumably – some limes tossed into the pot, and then maybe a little water. But I think water was carried in a kudam to the temple by another man. This mud pot was hoisted onto the shoulder of a man who had been holding one of the Devi’s swords – he was himself anointed in much the same way as the pot. Carried it out and back to the VB temple, with men along the way pouring water to cool the path. Pot carried into the garbagriha.

After this, an abhishekam to a silver sword happens. Starts with Sandanadi Thailam, abhisheka podi, then rice flour which is unique. After that all the usual oblations, but the swarnabhishekam happens with coins physically being poured and then a few ornaments also offered. The crowd is large, the mandapam (with images of Kailaiyam plastered on the wall) is packed. People are kind, they make room for us – two men hold their hands and allow me to sit and take photos outside the garba griha after the pot has been placed there, a kaappu for me. An older man there is the one who gives me information about the origins of the priest and what happens etc. The temple priests as such seem less involved. He tells me the sword will stand on the pot by a mechanism nobody can fathom, and it remains till night. After that, they take maavu (rice flour) and then go on a veethi ula, perhaps going back to the Murugan temple and then coming “home” after. Anyone can come see, but nobody should wear black – or else the sword falls down.
After abhishekam, the doors close and the sword is placed. Unclear how it’s made to stand, but it does. We get our darshan and leave.
Very entrancing energy around there as the Katthi Poduthal goes on. Self-inflicted Self-surrender.

Gopuja. Cow seems new, not used to this. Cow represents/contains all 33cr gods.The back is Mahalakshmi, front is her sister Moodevi (whose name should not be said), so the puja is always at the back and not the front. I heard a lot of “Kama” in the recitations, but maybe it was always Kamadhenu so the priest probably thought my question about this mighty stupid.
Kamadhenu is also well-known through its other five forms: Nanda, Sunanda, Surabhi, Susheela and Sumana. Also Kamaduha, Surabhi.

Astra homam, done by Arasoo mama after the conclusion of the other abhishekams–while the other priest attended to the homam. A recording is on drive.

Arasoo also sang the Abhirami padhigam (verse 1 after Vinayakar kaappu) beautifully. Partial recording on drive. Explained here. Also Sung here in Kaapi. Sirkazhi Govindarajan also has a 1970 film rendition.
