notes.title: Thiruvilakku Decoration and a Lying Down Ambal Alankaram
body: The security guard saw us and called us in from the road, I kid you not! It was hard not to stop, because the lying down utsavar right in front there looked very pleasing. The usual bevy of ladies gathered, chatting, reading, chanting. The Iyer doing his chants apparently in parallel. And along the whole left prakaram, rows of benches with numbered decorated lamps. My favourites were the one with the lime head and the roses for hair (many had pre-made faces, this did not), and the one that used ficus leaves to make a vinayaka form. Not sure which got the prizes though!

notes.title: It’s Not Only Kannika Parameswari with the Long Navaratri …
body: The Naga Mutthu Amman Koyil just down the street from the Kanyaka’s temple started its Vizha on October 11 like all others, but continues it well past – with a Mahishasura Samharam scheduled for October 28th! We asked about the temple and why this Samharam didn’t happen on Dashami – and were told that there’s a difference between the samharam and ambu poduthal, though I couldn’t understand what this was.

This is a theruvu koyil, but it’s been around a while. The last kumbabhishekam patrikai was 1968, said the man whose shrine it is, and the temple has been there a hundred years before that. He’s the third generation of caretakers. From Navaratri’s beginning, they take the 3rd Friday and keep the Samharam event for the Wednesday just prior.

There were a pambaikarar and a percussionist singing and telling stories, and nobody else present – even those whose houses adjoined knew little about the temple and were clearly having their own parallel conversations. We might check out the Samharam event, let’s see.

notes.title: An Abhishekam (or Two) a Day…
body: We were the only ones aside from the single ubhayakarar at this morning’s Kannika Parameswari Krittikkai Abhishekam. The usual dravyangal—oil, water (lots of it), abhisheka podi, 2 litres of milk, curd, 3 elaneer, rice flour, chandanam to be mixed with rose water. The priest works alone as usual, and chants the Purusha sultan, as well as Durga suktam and other verses I cannot make out, though Arun hears “Hayagreeva” at one point. The alankara is simple-velli kavacham and flowers. It’s much like the vinayaka Abhishekam I had seen for sankatahara chaturti, with gomathi masi. A no fuss affair. Small puja after and thinal or foxtail millet payasam. Traditionally made for Murugan this time of year, said the Iyer, a little makes a whole bucket. As we are leaving, they are calling the ladies filling the garbage truck outside to come in and have some.

In the evening is an arati thattu competition— to be fashioned out of coconut leaves. So all the women’s entries are being registered when we arrive at 645pm, between the Sivan and Nandhikeswara krittikkais. There will be a judging later. The nirvagam head’s wife comes to explain to me the rules, as she has seen us there often. Today is the last vidayattri day, so there is an extra air of festivity and perhaps a sense of relief. 17 days!! 17 days you’ve also enjoyed — says the lady who is active at the mahila sangam, who is always kind to us. Indeed.

There’s a second Abhishekam to Murugan going on. The morning one was early—Krithikai really only starts in the evening, we are not even really sure why the morning one happened, but depending on the ubhayakaras sometimes there can more than one in the day.
The utsavar was out, though I completely forgot to ask what alankaram today she wore!

notes.title: Murugan’s Day at Nandhikeswara
body: Not much to say about Nandhikeswara Krittikai except that it’s as well done as everything this temple undertakes! Abhishekam happens at 530pm, though this time may vary depending on when the nakshatram itself commences on the day. Alankaram takes a while, though it’s really simple and lovely, and you see the full brass figures dressed up. Then there’s an ul-purappadu, heralded by just the Nadaswaram and tavil.

notes.title: Arohara Sounds at Vedapuriswara
body: The Sivan Koyil krittikai process is Abhishekam for Murugan, and Pazhani Andavar. Did not seem like Vinayaka had an Abhishekam. But the deeparadhanai starts with Vinayaka, then Pazhani Andavar & finally an alangarified Murugan (whose face was white with vibhuti today). It’s all supposed to happen at 330pm, but then seems to finish in a rush at 530 when we get there. Meantime, utsavar is getting ready. Very simple and elegant alankaram (why not have this all the time?) with beautiful dhoti and saris tied. 7pm is the ul-purappadu, for which a decent crowd gathers.
Oh, and it’s Tuesday, so the Rahi Kalam Durga puja has happened, and the ladies are doing their parayanam in the evening as usual.

notes.title: Drama at Kannika Parameswari’s Doorstep
body: We’d been noticing, on the way to-from Kannika Parameswari’s many Navaratri days, that this littlest of theruvu koyils which had featured in our very first video on the temples of Pondicherry had a keeth shelter built outside and were doing pujas all through Naaratri. Never to big crowds at all, but doing them nonetheless. And they were continuing beyond Vijayadashami so we stopped by one day and found, to our surprise, quite a long schedule of events that, indeed, extended well beyond Navaratri. In fact, Vijayadashami’s key event, which is the slaying of Mahishasura, happens at this temple days after Dashami. Nobody really could explain why – “that day is for putting the ambu,” people said, “this is for Mahishasura’s Samharam” – not for a moment considering that the two are in fact one.

The swami purappadu would have started by 6pm, but we timed it to reach there at 830pm. It was perfect. A truck with a large cut-out figure stood near the temple, a distance from the cutting where the Utsavar was about to arrive, and was soon lit up from below. Amman as Durga, hair spread wide as though it was flying, hand on her trident, was in blazing red and coming down Kamatchi Amman Koyil St. just at the MG Road cutting. Two folk theatre performers came ahead of her, apparently gearing to go. A Thirunangai (transgender woman), and a man dressed much like Vallaraja at the Angalamman Mayana Kollai events earlier in the year. The pambaikarars arrive, and someone pulls a rope across the road. The Thirunangai (we’ll call her Durga from now on) stands on one side, in her red sari girdled with neem bunches, painted face and with her trident in hand. The Mahishasura figure, in his tights, skirt-like outfit and strange triangular hat and epaulettes, looking much like a burlesque figure, stood on the other. Then commenced the storytelling and the ritual re-enactment.

9 times Mahishasura comes, threatens, postures. 9 times, Durga battles him, with greater or lesser force, getting more and more tired each time and needing to be caught and resuscitated by the men tending to her, and failing, falling back. When she does, Mahishasura jumps back on the truck carrying the cut-out figure which has (we see now) detachable heads, switched out each time. First to come is Sooran, then Mahishasura (with a green buffalo head), the puli (tiger), the horse, the singham (lion, who looks like a horrifying cartoon character), the crocodile, the elephant, a bhootam like figure, a three-headed figure with Perumal namams, nama pola (or potta?) Sooran–and then finally Deception Himself in the form of the Atma lingam which must perforce be destroyed so the truth of the Atma Lingam can be retained. Each time he retreats, there is a burst of fire crackers (which some men on the side are coordinating)--not very loud ones, but enough to show his fiery retreat.

He recovers soon enough, he pushes the Goddess to her limits, but each time she summons the energy and she dances, round-round-round-round, and pushes her trident against him. 9 times he escapes. But the 10th time, when no less than the Atma Lingam is at stake–She strikes, Mahishasura falls, and the ignorance that he represents is reabsorbed into Her form.

A small deeparadhanai is done, and the whole procession flows forward once more to the temple. A small crowd has gathered, and it disperses. The Kannika staff and priest are at the temple entryway, watching. I think they close the temple rather later than usual this evening, because the drama at its doorstep draws their attention.
The Naga Muttu Amman Vizha goes on until November 2, finishing with an Unjal Utsavam. Sedal Utsavam is on October 30, but we won’t be able to attend. The full patrikai is in our photo files.
